newsitem.title: USA: Lockheed to build "smart kits" for U.S. bombs.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed to build "smart kits" for U.S. bombs.

text.p: The U.S. Air Force on Monday selected Lockheed Martin Corp. to produce 40,000 smart tail kits for special bombs in a $500 million programme to sharply increase the accuracy of the anti-armour weapons.
The "munitions-dispenser" bombs would carry different types of explosives such as mines that they would sow across battlefields and airfields against tanks and other equipment.

Lockheed Martin won a competition with Alliant Techsystems Inc. to produce the tail kits. The bombs will use global positioning satellites and adjustable tail fins to compensate for wind and other factors after they are dropped from high altitude by U.S. warplanes.

The Air Force said the first 40 tail kits will be delivered this spring and the weapons would be initially assigned to B-52 bombers and F-16 attack jets. Later, they will be used by radar-evading F-117A "stealth" fighters, F-15E attack jets and big B-1 bombers.
Asst. Air Force Secretary Arthur Money said the "wind corrected munitions dispenser" programme, which was begun after the 1991 Gulf War, has been extremely successful.

Other service officials said the munition carriers, which are different from bombs now guided to their targets by laser beam, will result in high accuracy even if they are dropped from altitudes of 30,000 feet (10,000 metres) out of the range of anti-aircraft weapons.

Lockheed Martin was awarded a $21 million contract to get the programme going, but the Air Force said that follow-on production contracts for the tail kits are expected to increase the total programme to about $500 million.
